summary: Asked whether a vote could cost support, a member explains why they will stand by it.
realLife: Pennsylvania Representative Marjorie Margolies-Mezvinsky backed the 1993 budget after opposing it publicly. She later recalled weighing her seat against the president’s program, and her next opponent campaigned on that vote.
inGame: press-comment reads the vote and electorateSides for the underlying question.
gates: There is a recorded vote and evidence of electoral disagreement.

turns.what: The member explains the vote and leaves its effect on the next election open.
turns.pulledBy: No election or reliable measure of support has followed the vote.
turns.writesBack: The interview records the position without assigning an electoral loss.

turns.what: At a district meeting months later, a voter produces the member’s old pledge and asks when she changed her mind.
turns.pulledBy: The office has a dated pledge and a subsequent roll call on the same measure.
turns.writesBack: The district staff file the question with the vote so the next town hall can return to it.
